stem_text: A body of mass 2 kg is driven by an engine delivering a constant power of 1 J/s. The body starts from rest and moves in a straight line. After 9 seconds, the body has moved a distance (in m) _______.

candidate_solve.derivation: Mass m = 2 kg, constant power P = 1 J/s. From work-energy theorem, P*t = 0.5*m*v^2 => (1)*t = 0.5*(2)*v^2 => v(t) = t^(1/2). Displacement x = int_0^t v(t') dt' = int_0^9 t'^(1/2) dt' = (2/3)*[t^(3/2)]_0^9 = (2/3)*(27) = 18 m.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Connecting constant engine power to kinetic energy and integrating non-linear velocity profile

representation_translation.evidence: Integrating v(t) = sqrt(2Pt/m) over time to derive straight-line displacement

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Find v(t) from Pt = 0.5*m*v^2, evaluate definite integral x(t) = int_0^9 v(t')dt', compute x(9)

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Evaluating fractional power 9^(3/2) = 27 and multiplying (2/3)*27 = 18 m

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Recognizing acceleration is non-constant; standard kinematic equations v=u+at cannot be used

demand_proposal.rationale: Applying calculus integration to constant power velocity function under rectilinear motion
